chain.g: to be on one's guard, be vigilant

ety.text: From Middle English bewar, be war, be ware, forms of Middle English ben ware (“to be on one's guard, be vigilant”, literally “be ware”), equivalent to be + ware or be + aware. Compare Old English bewarian.

senses.d: To use caution, pay attention to (used both with and without of).
ex: Behold, I send an Angel before thee[…]. Beware of him, and obey his voice.

fr:faire attention.gl: to pay attention, to be careful

chain.g: to fear, be afraid of, apprehend, be apprehensive of

ety.text: Inherited from Latin timēre. Compare Portuguese and Spanish temer.

it:fare attenzione.gl: to look out; to stay aware; to beware

pt:tomar cuidado.gl: to watch out; to take care (to use caution)
